title: Quantifying the Surface Sensitivity of Atomic Resolution Secondary Electron Imaging
content: Secondary electron (SE) imaging is a surface sensitive imaging method that complements traditional scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). Atomic resolution secondary electron (SE) was first demonstrated in 2009 using an aberration corrected (AC) STEM, and since then has been the topic of numerous experimental and theoretical studies [1-4]. Recently, it was shown that atomic resolution is retained in SE images of bulk specimens where STEM imaging is not feasible [5]. This raises the attractive possibility of imaging the surfaces of materials without requiring the special sample preparation that STEM usually does. Of particular interest is the question of exactly how surface sensitive secondary electron imaging is, and whether one could image the surface monolayer of a bulk substrate. While there has been previous work on secondary electron mean free paths (MFPs) in monolayers [6-8], there is a dearth of material specific information.
